main_text.l: & vinum lymphatum in Missis haberi mandauit, aliaq; plura constituit. Affert tamē Baptista Mat-tuanus in 6. Fastorum libro, Azyma seu fuerint, sicut dixere Pelasgi, Liba, quibus fecit sacri venerabilis author, Ambiguum celebrare modo laudabile utroq; si nostrae finerent leges, Romanaq; iura.

Mortem Clemens anno Domini 1191. operibus his insistens, obiit. In praedicta cleri reformatione, Cardinalem quendam in Poloniam misit, qui corrigens clericorum mores, synodum illic congregauit. In qua caelibatum unctis suis praecepit: & pro recuperanda terra sancta decimas dari monuit. Chron. Pol. lib. 3. cap. 26. Danorum plebs suis facer dotibus coniugia decernens, ab hoc pontifice excommunicabatur. Saxo Gram. libro 15.

Coelestinus tertius, natione Romanus, patre Petro Bubonis, & Iacynthus antea dictus: uir senex, in festo Paschae post Clementis mortem, per Cardinales & episcopos inauguratus, sequenti die Imperatorem Henricum sextum coronauit. Qui aegre ferens Tancredum Siciliae regno potiri (ars[?] vere pontificia) eidem Imperatori Constantiam monacham, Rogerij filiam, e monasterio Panormitano eductam[?], uxorem dedit, ea conditione, ut dotis

page.notes: The printed text is partly damaged at the right edge and at the foot of the page. The word "eductam" in the last full line is hard to read and may be a different word. "ars" in the parenthesis is doubtful. The printed ligatures & and "ct" were taken as read. The running head and the capital headings were set with the u/v rule applied to the capitals (U for vowel, V for consonant), so the printed VM and VS appear as UM and US.
